experimental_procedure: In a typical procedure, the oxime (0.3-1 mmol) was dissolved in the IL (about 1 mL) and added, under stirring, with the appropriate quantity of cyanuric chloride (TCT, 2 or 20 mol%). The mixture was left at the desired temperature (60 °C or 130 °C) and monitored by TLC (eluant EtOAc-light PE) until completion. The amide was isolated by direct chromatography (silica gel) of the reaction mixture (eluant EtOAc-light PE). Alternatively, the mixture was extracted with MTBE (4 × 3 mL) and concentrated under vacuum. The crude was purified on silica gel column to afford the pure product. The amide was identified (1H NMR) by comparison with the authentic sample. The residue of the IL was dissolved in CH2Cl2, filtered on Celite, and reused after removal of the organic solvent under vacuum. Table 1, entry 1, yield 99%.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Atypical reaction was carried out in a closed glass tube. The oxime (1 mmol) was weighed into the tube and dissolved in 2 mL dry CH3CN. Subsequently, 26 mg (0.05 mmol) of gallium triflate was added to give a homogeneous reaction mixture. In the cases of less reactive substrates, larger amounts of catalysts (up to 50 mol%) were used (Table 1). The tube was heated to the desired temperature and the reaction mixture was periodically monitored by TLC (silica gel, CH2Cl2/CH3OH mixtures) for completion of the reaction. The mixture was cooled at the end of the reaction. In some cases, the product precipitated and was easily separated by filtration followed by washing with a small amount of acetonitrile. Otherwise, the reaction mixture was quenched with water and extracted using diethyl ether (three to five times). The combined organics were dried over anhydrous magnesium sulfate and then solvents were removed at reduced pressure to give the crude product. In most cases, product was almost pure and directly characterized by GC-MS and NMR. Otherwise, the products were purified by column chromatography (silica gel, CH2Cl2/CH3OH mixtures) before analysis. Yield 94%.

After completion of the reaction as monitored by TLC, the reaction was quenched with saturated aqueous NaHCO3 (10 mL) and the product was extracted with ethyl acetate (10 mL x 3). authors: Tarkin-Tas, Eylem; Mathias, Lon J.

experimental_procedure: Synthesis of 5-Azepane-2-one Ethylene Ketal (2). Oxime 1 (60 mmol) was dissolved in 170 mL of acetone in a 500 mL round-bottomed flask charged with a magnetic stirrer. Addition of 60 mL of 4 N aqueous NaOH solution was followed by slow addition of p-toluenesulfonoyl chloride (108 mmol) dissolved in 170 mL of acetone. The reaction mixture was allowed to mix 2 h at room temperature. After the evaporation of acetone 40mL of H2O was added. The reaction mixture was then neutralized by dropwise addition of 4 N aqueous HCl solution. The reaction was allowed to proceed overnight at room temperature. The reaction mixture was transferred into an extraction funnel, and the product was separated by extraction with CH2Cl2 (5 x 200 mL). Combined organic phases were dried over anhydrous Na2SO4 and filtered, and the solvent was evaporated. 5-Azepane-2-one ethylene ketal, KLCL (9.6 g, 93%), was recrsytallized twice from acetone. mp 104 °C. Anal. Calcd for C8H13NO3; C: 56.13 H: 7.65 N: 8.18. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Atypical reaction was carried out in a closed glass tube. The oxime (1 mmol) was weighed into the tube and dissolved in 2 mL dry CH3CN. Subsequently, 26 mg (0.05 mmol) of gallium triflate was added to give a homogeneous reaction mixture. In the cases of less reactive substrates, larger amounts of catalysts (up to 50 mol%) were used (Table 1). The tube was heated to the desired temperature and the reaction mixture was periodically monitored by TLC (silica gel, CH2Cl2/CH3OH mixtures) for completion of the reaction. The mixture was cooled at the end of the reaction. In some cases, the product precipitated and was easily separated by filtration followed by washing with a small amount of acetonitrile. Otherwise, the reaction mixture was quenched with water and extracted using diethyl ether (three to five times). The combined organics were dried over anhydrous magnesium sulfate and then solvents were removed at reduced pressure to give the crude product. In most cases, product was almost pure and directly characterized by GC-MS and NMR. Otherwise, the products were purified by column chromatography (silica gel, CH2Cl2/CH3OH mixtures) before analysis. experimental_procedure: 4-Ethoxy-6,7-dihydro-1H-azepin-2(5H)-one. A solution of methanesulfonyl chloride (2.1 mL, 26.5 mmol) in dichloromethane (27 mL) was added dropwise via cannula to a solution of oxime (2.74 g, 17.7 mmol) and triethylamine (3.7 mL, 26.5 mmol) in CH2Cl2 (40 mL) at 0 °C. Upon completion of addition, the cloudy solution was diluted with CH2Cl2 (50 mL) and poured onto ice-cold water (100 mL). The mixture was extracted with dichloromethane (3 x 50 mL), and the combined organic extracts were dried (Na2SO4) and concentrated in vacuo to afford a yellow oil, which was diluted with benzene (15 mL) and loaded immediately onto a column of neutral alumina. The oil was left on the column for 12 h and was eluted sequentially with hexane (200 mL), benzene (150 mL), and methanol (200 mL). The product was eluted from the column with the methanol fraction and the methanol was removed in vacuo. The resulting yellow residue was diluted with dichloromethane (50 mL) and was washed with 5% aqueous sodium bicarbonate (50 mL), and the mixture was extracted with CH2Cl2 (3 x 30 mL). The combined organic extracts were dried (Na2SO4), filtered, and concentrated in vacuo to afford the crude product 4-Ethoxy-6,7-dihydro-1H-azepin-2(5H)-one, yellow solid, yield 2.4 g, 87%. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) d 6.52 (br s, NH), 5.07 (s, 1H), 3.80 (q, J = 7.0 Hz, 2H), 3.23 (m, 2H), 2.49 (t, J = 7.0 Hz, 2H), 1.96 (m, 2H), 1.32 (t, J = 7.0 Hz, 3H); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3) d 172.3, 167.9, 96.6, 63.5, 41.1, 32.7, 27.0, 14.3; IR (neat) νmax 3260, 2986, 2975, 2931, 1675, 1587, 1460, 1428, 1352, 1244, 1163, 1119 cm-1; HRMS (ESI) m/z calcd for C8H13NO2Na: 178.0844; found: 178.0840.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Sulfamic acid (0.3 mmol) and zinc chloride (0.2 mmol) were added to a solution of ketoxime (1 mmol) in acetonitrile (3 mL). The mixture was heated to reflux (90 °C) for the period as indicated in Table 3. The progress of the reaction was monitored by thin-layer chromatography (TLC). After the completion of the reaction, the reaction was dispersed into 10mL cooled diethyl ether to precipitate sulfamic acid. The resulting suspension was filtered to recycle sulfamic acid. The combined organic layer was dried over anhydrous magnesium sulfate and filtered. To a solution of 2-tert-butylcyclohexanone oxime (339 mg, 2 mmol in 5 mL acetonitrile) in a two-necked flask equipped with reflux condenser under nitrogen atmosphere, was added mercury(II) chloride (165 mg, 0.6 mmol). After being stirred at 80°C for 8 hr, the reaction mixture was allowed to cool and then acetonitrile (5 mL) was added to dissolve the solid formed. title: An efficient and versatile one-pot Beckmann rearrangement of ketoximes using mesitylenesulfonyl chloride
authors: Ramalingan, Chennan; Park, Yong-Tae
reference: An efficient and versatile one-pot Beckmann rearrangement of ketoximes using mesitylenesulfonyl chloride | Ramalingan, Chennan; Park, Yong-Tae | Synthesis (2008), (9), 1351-1358
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Rearrangement of Ketoximes into Lactams/Amides; General Procedure To a solution of oxime (1.5 mmol) in THF (4 mL) in a two-necked flask equipped with reflux condenser and addition funnel under nitrogen atmosphere, was added LiOH (1.8 mmol). After being stirred for 30 min at r.t., a solution of mesitylenesulfonyl chloride (1.5 mmol) in THF (4 mL) was added and stirring was continued for 1 h at ambient temperature followed by 60 °C until the reaction was complete (monitored by TLC). The reaction was allowed to cool and quenched by addition of H2O (10 mL). The solvents were removed under reduced pressure and then H2O (15 mL) and Et2O (15 mL) were added. The organic phase was separated and the aqueous phase was extracted with Et2O (2 × 15 mL). The combined organic phases were washed with brine (2 × 10 mL), dried over Na2SO4 and filtered. The crude product obtained after evaporation of the filtrate was purified by flash column chromatography (CH2Cl2-MeOH, 100:2) to provide the lactam/amide. N-(2-Bromophenyl)acetamide (4c, Table 3, Entry 3)17, yield 83%. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3): δ = 8.31 (d, J = 8.5 Hz, 1 H), 7.68 (br s, 1 H), 7.54 (dd, J = 8.0, 1.5 Hz, 1 H), 7.31 (dt, J = 1.3, 8.0 Hz, 1 H), 6.99 (t, J = 7.3 Hz, 1 H), 2.25 (s, 3 H).

title: Organocatalyzed Beckmann Rearrangement of Cyclohexanone Oxime in a Microchemical System
authors: Zhang, Jisong; Dong, Chen; Du, Chencan; Luo, Guangsheng
reference: Organocatalyzed Beckmann Rearrangement of Cyclohexanone Oxime in a Microchemical System | Zhang, Jisong; Dong, Chen; Du, Chencan; Luo, Guangsheng | Organic Process Research & Development (2015), 19(2), 352-356
experimental_procedure: Equipment. A schematic overview of the microreaction system is shown in Figure 6. In the experiment, TFA and COX which was dissolved in acetonitrile were both delivered by metering pumps (Beijing Satellite Co. Ltd.). The mixing was performed in a microvolume T-shaped mixer (Beijing Mingnike Analytical Instrument Center). The micromixer is made of PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) material with an inner diameter of 0.25 mm. The reactants were pumped through the pipes immersed in an oil bath to control the feeding temperature. A delay loop (PTFE) immersed in the oil bath with an inner diameter of 2 mm and an external diameter of 3 mm was connected directly downstream to the Micromixer 1 to control the residence time. The residence time could be controlled accurately by changing the length of the delay loop or the flow velocity. The pressure was controlled at 0.6 MPa by a metering valve (Beijing Xiongchuan Technology Ltd.) at the outlet right after the Micromixer 2. During the experiments, it was found that nearly no vaporization occurred in the microsystem even at the high temperature of 130 °C. In order to control residence time accurately, Micromixer 2 was designed to quench the reaction by adding a large amount of acetonitrile to the reacting system. Ronchin et al.14 has described the kinetics of the rearrangement by TFA in acetonitrile at 90 °C. The conversion of COX reached only 15% with the reaction time of 50 min and TFA concentration of 1 mol/L. Thus, we can figure out that the reaction in the mixtures (TFA concentration <1 mol/L) is stopped after the dilution of acetonitrile at room temperature. During the experiments, the acetonitrile solution and TFA were pumped into Micromixer 1 to induce the rearrangement reaction and then reaction went on in the delay loop. A large amount of acetonitrile was pumped into Micromixer 2 to quench the reaction by both cooling and dilution of reaction mixture. After about 5 min, the system was stable, and then the samples were collected directly at the outlet. The sampling time was also recorded with a stopwatch.

After being stirred for 30 min at r.t., a solution of mesitylenesulfonyl chloride (1.5 mmol) in THF (4 mL) was added and stirring was continued for 1 h at ambient temperature followed by 60 °C until the reaction was complete (monitored by TLC). title: Mercury-Catalyzed Rearrangement of Ketoximes into Amides and Lactams in Acetonitrile
authors: Ramalingan, Chennan; Park, Yong-Tae
reference: Mercury-Catalyzed Rearrangement of Ketoximes into Amides and Lactams in Acetonitrile | Ramalingan, Chennan; Park, Yong-Tae | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2007), 72(12), 4536-4538
experimental_procedure: Synthesis of N-(2-chlorophenyl)acetamide (Table 3, entry 11). 7 To a solution of 1-(2- chlorophenyl)ethanone oxime (170 mg, 1 mmol in 5 mL acetonitrile) in a two-necked flask equipped with reflux condenser under nitrogen atmosphere, was added mercury(II) chloride (33 mg, 0.12 mmol). After being stirred at 80°C for 8 hr, the reaction mixture was allowed to cool and then acetonitrile (5 mL) was added to dissolve the solid formed. The solvent was stripped off and the organic material was taken up in dichloromethane (4x10 mL). The combined organic layers were washed with brine, dried over magnesium sulphate, and filtered. The filtrate was evaporated under reduced pressure and the residue obtained was purified by flash-column chromatography over silica gel (230-400 mesh) with a dichloromethanemethanol (100:4) eluent system to afford N-(2-chlorophenyl)acetamide as an off-white solid (141 mg, 83%). mp 90-91°C. 1H NMR δH(400 MHz; CDCl3; Me4Si; 25°C) 8.34 (1H, d, J = 8.04Hz), 7.65 (1H, br.s), 7.35 (1H, dd, J = 8.02Hz; 1.50Hz), 7.28-7.24 (1H, m), 7.03 (1H, t, J = 7.28Hz), 2.23 (3H, s).

title: Gallium (III) Triflate Catalyzed Beckmann Rearrangement
authors: Yan, Ping; Batamack, Patrice; Prakash, G. K. Surya; Olah, George A.
reference: Gallium (III) Triflate Catalyzed Beckmann Rearrangement | Yan, Ping; Batamack, Patrice; Prakash, G. K. Surya; Olah, George A. | Catalysis Letters (2005), 103(3-4), 165-168
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Atypical reaction was carried out in a closed glass tube. The oxime (1 mmol) was weighed into the tube and dissolved in 2 mL dry CH3CN. Subsequently, 26 mg (0.05 mmol) of gallium triflate was added to give a homogeneous reaction mixture. In the cases of less reactive substrates, larger amounts of catalysts (up to 50 mol%) were used (Table 1). The tube was heated to the desired temperature and the reaction mixture was periodically monitored by TLC (silica gel, CH2Cl2/CH3OH mixtures) for completion of the reaction. The mixture was cooled at the end of the reaction. In some cases, the product precipitated and was easily separated by filtration followed by washing with a small amount of acetonitrile. Otherwise, the reaction mixture was quenched with water and extracted using diethyl ether (three to five times). The combined organics were dried over anhydrous magnesium sulfate and then solvents were removed at reduced pressure to give the crude product. In most cases, product was almost pure and directly characterized by GC-MS and NMR. Otherwise, the products were purified by column chromatography (silica gel, CH2Cl2/CH3OH mixtures) before analysis. Yield 92%.

title: Microwave induced bismuth trichloride catalysed beckmann rearrangement of oximes
authors: Thakur, Ashim J.; Boruah, Anima; Prajapati, Dipak; Sandhu, Jagir S.
reference: Microwave induced bismuth trichloride catalysed beckmann rearrangement of oximes | Thakur, Ashim J.; Boruah, Anima; Prajapati, Dipak; Sandhu, Jagir S. | Synthetic Communications (2000), 30(12), 2105-2111
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Beckmann Rearrangement of oximes :- Benzophenone oxime 1 (R=Ph, 10 mmol) and bismuth trichloride9 (12 mmol) were mixed together in an Erlenmeyer flask and placed in a commercial microwave oven (operating at 2450 MHz frequency) and irradiated for 8 minutes. The reaction mixture was allowed to reach room temperature, treated with 20% sodium bicarbonate solution and extracted with dichloromethane and dried over anhydrous sodium sulphate. Removal of solvent and the residue on purification by column chromatography on silica gel gave the corresponding benzanilide in 90% yield and there was no evidence for. the formation of any deoximated products. Similar treatment of 2-methyleyclohexanone and 1-tetralone oximes gave the corresponding ring expanded rearranged products in 75-80% yields as summerised in the table and their characteristics are recorded here. 2h, yield 75%. 1H NMR 2.38 (m, 4H, CH2), 3.08 (m, 2H, CH2), 7.10-7.30 (m, 4H, ArH) and 9.50 (1H, NH); IR (KBr) 3180, 3060, 1700 cm-1; MS m/e 161 (M+). Anal. Calcd. (found) for C10H11NO C.74.53 (74.62); H, 6.83 (6.90); N, 8.69 (8.74).
